author: Mohammad Yeasin
subject: grammar
title: Past Continuous Tense
intro_blurb: The Past Continuous Tense is used to describe actions that were in progress at a specific moment in the past. It is essential for storytelling, describing background scenes, and talking about interrupted actions. In this lesson, you will learn the rules, Bangla explanation, examples, common mistakes, and practice exercises.
learning_outcomes: Understand when to use the Past Continuous
Talk about actions in progress at a past time

timeline.description: I was sleeping at 10 pm. (action in progress at a specific past moment)

comparison.usage: Action in progress at a specific time in the past
Completed action at a specific time in the past

common_mistakes.explanation: Use 'verb-ing' after was/were, not the past participle.

audio_examples: She was reading a book at 8 pm.
They were playing football when it started to rain.
I was cooking dinner while he was watching TV.
speaking_practice: She was cooking when the phone rang.
They were not listening to the teacher.
Were you watching TV at 8 pm?
He was reading a newspaper while I was writing.

quiz.question: Which is the correct sentence?
quiz.explanation: Use 'was' for I/He/She/It, and 'verb-ing' for the action.

quiz.question: Fill in the blank: She _____ (read) a book at 8 pm.
Correct the sentence: I were sleeping when he called.
quiz.answer: I was sleeping when he called.

quiz.question: Translate to English: সে রাত ১০টায় ঘুমাচ্ছিল।

faq.q: When do we use the Past Continuous?
faq.a: For actions that were in progress at a specific time in the past.

faq.q: What is the difference between Past Continuous and Past Simple?
faq.a: Past Continuous describes an ongoing action; Past Simple describes a completed action.
Use 'was' for I/He/She/It, and 'were' for You/We/They.

faq.q: Can I use 'yesterday' with Past Continuous?
faq.a: Yes, if you specify a time: 'I was sleeping at 10 pm yesterday.'
While, when, at that time, as, at 8 pm, yesterday at 5 o'clock.
